Add the missing unit-periods of a panel as rows

Source: R/fill_panel.R
fill_panel.Rd

The fix for a panel that ensure_balanced() reports: every unit-period that should be there and is not becomes a row, with the unit and the period filled in and every other column missing. A count of persons per year then counts a person who is missing in a year as missing, instead of leaving the year out, and a lag over years compares the years it should.

Usage

fill_panel(data, id, time, periods = NULL, gaps_only = TRUE, flag = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr or c(cvr, lbnr).

time

The period column (one column), e.g. year. Any type that sorts, such as integer years or dates.

periods

Expected periods. Defaults to the periods observed in data.

gaps_only

If TRUE (default), only periods between a unit's first and last observation are added. If FALSE, every unit gets every period.

flag

Name of a logical column marking the added rows, or NULL (default) for none.

Value

data with the missing unit-periods added: a tibble for a data frame, a query for a database or Arrow table.

Details

It is the one fix for a panel that needs no choice: the missing rows are given by the unit and the periods, and their values are unknown. It does not guess them; carry a status forward with carry_status() if that is what the analysis needs.

The fix is never silent: it says how many rows it added, and for how many units. With flag, the added rows are marked in a logical column of that name, so they can be found afterwards.

The periods and gaps_only work as in ensure_balanced(): by default a unit gets the periods between its first and last observation, so a person who enters late or leaves early is not given rows before birth or after death. With gaps_only = FALSE every unit gets every period.

A data frame comes back with the added rows sorted in among the others, by unit and period. A database or Arrow table comes back as a query that adds the rows, without changing the table.

See also

ensure_balanced() and describe_panel() to find the gaps first.

Examples

panel <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b"),
  year   = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2022),
  income = c(100, 110, 120, 90, 95)
)
# b lacks 2021
fill_panel(panel, cpr, year)
#> ℹ Added 1 row for 1 unit, with every column but cpr, year missing.
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   cpr    year income
#>   <chr> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 a      2020    100
#> 2 a      2021    110
#> 3 a      2022    120
#> 4 b      2020     90
#> 5 b      2021     NA
#> 6 b      2022     95

fill_panel(panel, cpr, year, flag = "filled")
#> ℹ Added 1 row for 1 unit, with every column but cpr, year missing.
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   cpr    year income filled
#>   <chr> <dbl>  <dbl> <lgl> 
#> 1 a      2020    100 FALSE 
#> 2 a      2021    110 FALSE 
#> 3 a      2022    120 FALSE 
#> 4 b      2020     90 FALSE 
#> 5 b      2021     NA TRUE  
#> 6 b      2022     95 FALSE
